reasoning_input.question_text: Prove by mathematical induction that 2ⁿ > n² for all integers n ≥ 5.

student_steps.content: Base case (n = 5): LHS = 2⁵ = 32; RHS = 5² = 25. 32 > 25 ✓ True for n = 5.
Inductive hypothesis: Assume true for n = k (k ≥ 5), i.e., 2ᵏ > k².
Target: Need to show true for n = k + 1, i.e., 2ᵏ⁺¹ > (k + 1)².
LHS for n = k + 1: 2ᵏ⁺¹ = 2 · 2ᵏ > 2 · k² = k² + k²  [using hypothesis 2ᵏ > k²]
Conclusion: Since statement holds for n = 5 and truth for n = k implies truth for n = k + 1, by mathematical induction 2ⁿ > n² for all integers n ≥ 5.

reasoning_input.final_answer: Proven by mathematical induction for all integers n ≥ 5

steps.description: Verify base case n = 5: LHS = 32 > 25 = RHS
State inductive hypothesis for n = k (2ᵏ > k² for k ≥ 5)
State target inequality for n = k + 1: 2ᵏ⁺¹ > (k + 1)²
